content:
maya: Hey team — saw a config change landed that tightened egress on the Dedicated VPCs. After that, a few private control-plane calls started failing (504s). Noticed it coincided with the RBAC refactor PR merged last night. Anyone tracking?
aj: I saw alerts. Which calls are failing exactly? control-plane agent -> KMS or to the metrics endpoint?
maya: Mostly the private control plane to our central KMS endpoint and the egress IPs to the metrics ingest. Example error from control-plane logs:
```
org.redwood.controlplane.rpc.RpcException: connection timed out to kms.redwood-infra.internal:443
at ...
Caused by: java.net.ConnectException: Network is unreachable
```
devops: Pinged infra, and firewall rules show a new deny for outbound range 10.20.0.0/21 that used to be allowed. That subnet contains our KMS NAT pool.
oliver: That deny came from the new role-bound egress policy rolled by the RBAC change — we moved egress permissions under role:deployment-owner, and default roles lost it. Looks like private-controlplane svcacct didn't inherit the role.
sre-oncall: Rolling impact: 3 private deploy customers hit brief API timeouts, auto-retries recovered most but we saw a spike in error budgets. Reproduced locally by forcing the service account to the new role and removing the egress allowance.
security-bot: Detector triggered: policy-change:rbac (PR #8421) merged by @kevin. Changed resources: egress-policies/* and role-bindings/*.
kevin: That's me. I merged the refactor; assumed all existing service accounts had explicit bindings. Didn’t realize some private-controlplane svcaccts were using inherited clusterroles. Sorry — my bad.
maya: Quick questions: 1) can we add a temporary egress allow for the KMS NAT IPs to unblock? 2) how do we fix role bindings so this doesn't reoccur? 3) audit logs — are we missing entries for the denied egress?
aj: For (1) we can patch fw rule in prod in ~5min. I'll do an emergency patch to re-open outbound to 10.20.5.0/24 for controlplane subnets.
devops: For (3) the cloud audit logs show CONNECT attempts but the iam audit doesn't show a role-binding change for those specific svcaccts because they were relying on inherited binding. We should add an explicit RoleBinding in private-controlplane namespace.
kevin: I'll open a PR to add explicit RoleBindings for private-controlplane service-accounts across Dedicated/Private fleets. Also adding an integration test to validate egress permissions after RBAC changes.
maya: Also KMS integration: some decrypt calls failed with 403 on the KMS proxy before timeouts. Could be token propagation lag when role binding dropped. Anyone seen KMS logs?
oliver: KMS logs show failed auth with reason: "service-account not authorized" at 2023-11-02T02:14:09Z for a handful of requests. After we re-applied the allowlist they succeeded.
sre-oncall: Action items I'm noting: 1) aj patches egress allowlist (in flight) 2) kevin opens PR to add explicit RoleBindings + integration test 3) devops run a sweep to find any svcacct relying on inherited egress-binding 4) oliver to verify KMS audit entries and export for compliance.
kevin: Will do PR + tests, ETA 3 hours. I’ll also add a pre-merge CI check that fails if an RBAC refactor touches egress-policies without a paired rolebinding update.
maya: For post-incident: we should add an audit alert that triggers if a role-binding removal coincides with increased egress denies for control-plane subnets. Might save time next time.
security-bot: Created incident ticket INC-2023-4127 and linked PRs.
aj: patch applied, confirmed connectivity restored to KMS and metrics. Monitoring looks stable.
maya: Thanks. Can someone paste the quick remediation commands for the runbook? I'll add to the private-deploy runbook.
devops: Runbook snippet:
```
# emergency reopen egress
kubectl -n infra patch egresspolicy allow-kms --type='json' -p='[{"op":"add","path":"/spec/allowedCIDRs/-","value":"10.20.5.0/24"}]'
# verify
curl -sS https://kms.redwood-infra.internal/health || true
```
kevin: After PR merges I'll run a scan across namespaces for svcacct missing explicit bindings and create tickets.
maya: OK closing here for now — follow-ups tracked in INC-2023-4127 and kevin's PR. Thanks for quick response :thumbsup:
